subject: EdgeTech dedicated capacity: tokens/sec, SLO fit & headroom
messages:
From: Bethany Ross <bethany@edgetech.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: Dedicated sizing: target tokens/sec and SLO questions

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers looked promising. We're starting internal budgeting and need a concrete sizing proposal for the Dedicated capacity line item in our procurement packet. Key asks:  

- Target steady-state tokens/sec to support our expected 1.2M monthly active users (estimated 25M tokens/day peak).
- Expected p95 and p99 latency per request for the chat flows (avg prompt + 400-token responses).
- Recommended GPU slabs and headroom assumptions for 1x, 3x, and seasonal 5x burst.
- Any fallback plans (smaller model variant) if we exceed committed capacity.

If you can send a short spreadsheet with tokens/sec mapping to GPU slabs + assumptions we can push to procurement. Timeline: procurement needs estimates by next Monday (2026-11-22).

Thanks —
Bethany Ross
Head of Platform Integrations
EdgeTech

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Bethany Ross <bethany@edgetech.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing: target tokens/sec and SLO questions

Hi Bethany —

Appreciate the clear asks. See the attached spreadsheet (capacity_model_v1.xlsx) for a first-pass mapping. High-level summary below:

- Steady-state target: 290 tokens/sec sustained per region to cover the projected daily peaks (maps to ~2.5B tokens/day sustained during business hours).
- p95 latency (chat, avg prompt + 400 tokens) estimate: 220–300 ms on A100 equivalent slabs with continuous batching and warmed KV cache. p99: 420–650 ms depending on input lengths.
- GPU slabs: we recommend reserving 8 A100-equivalent GPUs for the committed tier (handles ~300 tps with 20% headroom). For 3x growth reserve policy, add elastic burst capacity that can be auto-brokered (recommend 8 additional GPUs in Dedicated burst pool). For seasonal 5x spikes, plan a mixed strategy: short-term hosted fallback to large-context optimized variant + on-prem burst.
- Fallback: automatic routing to a quantized 8-bit variant of the model with toggled prefix caching; expected median latency +40% but cost reduced ~2.2x.

Asked the infra team to validate the slab assumptions below — Ben, Marissa, Jordan: can you confirm the tokens/sec -> GPU mapping in tab "Assumptions" and update any latency tail risks?

Attaching: capacity_model_v1.xlsx (columns: scenario, tokens_per_sec, GPUs_reserved, headroom_pct, fallback_plan).

Next steps: if these numbers look OK to you, we'll convert into a Mutual Action Plan and align on procurement milestones by 11/22.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Bethany Ross <bethany@edgetech.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T14:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing: target tokens/sec and SLO questions

Folks —

Quick validation from infra/ops perspective after running the capacity model against historical token distributions and a synthetic burst trace:

- Confirmed mapping: ~36k tokens/sec sustained per A100-equivalent GPU for the model profile you referenced (avg response length ~400 tokens, batch-friendly patterns). That yields ~300 tps across 8 GPUs with ~20% operational headroom.
- Tail risk: p99 can spike beyond 700 ms if the KV cache is cold and concurrent long-context sessions ramp quickly. Mitigations: proactive cache warm-up (prefetch common prefixes) and a 30-minute warm window during major marketing events.
- Burst handling: for 3x bursts, autoscaler can bring additional Ded. GPUs online in ~4–6 minutes depending on spare pool availability. For 5x spikes, fall back to hosted pools with cross-region redundancy — recommend contract clause to allow short-term hosted overflow at negotiated overage rate.

Attached: gpu_mapping_v2.csv (per-GPU throughput sims, latency tails by concurrency).

Marissa/Jordan — if you want to tweak the slab counts or present alternatives (e.g., more smaller GPUs vs fewer large ones) I can re-run sims.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

From: Bethany Ross <bethany@edgetech.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, EdgeTech Procurement <procurement@edgetech.ai>
Date: 2026-11-19T11:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing: target tokens/sec and SLO questions

Thanks team — this is helpful. A couple follow-ups before we sign off with procurement: 

1) Can you add a short section that maps committed tokens/sec to expected monthly bill variance if we use the hosted overflow option? Procurement needs worst-case cost exposure.
2) For the p95/p99 numbers, can you provide an assumed request size distribution (we have some users sending 800–1200 token prompts occasionally). How does that change your slab recommendation?

I've attached a draft procurement_timeline.pdf — procurement is targeting a signed PO by 12/10. If you can fold these two items into the Mutual Action Plan that would be great.

-Bethany
Bethany Ross
Head of Platform Integrations
EdgeTech

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Bethany Ross <bethany@edgetech.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, EdgeTech Procurement <procurement@edgetech.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T16:45:00Z
Subject: EdgeTech Mutual Action Plan + final headroom recs (ET-4339)

Hi Bethany & team —

Thanks for the patience. Per Priyom/Ben's inputs, we've consolidated a Mutual Action Plan (attached: mutual_action_plan.docx) and updated the capacity worksheet to include:

- Committed baseline: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (covers ~290 tokens/sec steady-state).
- p95 estimate (baseline request distro): 240–300 ms; p99 420–700 ms. If 10% of requests expand to 800–1200 tokens, p95 moves to ~380–480 ms and p99 to ~900–1,200 ms unless additional GPUs are provisioned.
- Headroom policy: keep 20% reserved headroom on committed slabs; 3x buffer via dedicated burst pool (8 GPUs) with 4–6 minute spin-up; 5x seasonal strategy uses hosted overflow (documented overage caps and negotiated 30-day credit window).
- Cost mapping: included a delta table showing expected monthly cost delta for hosted overflow at 1x/3x/5x scenarios (see M.A.P. sec 3). Procurement note: worst-case exposure (5x sustained for 7 days) triggers an estimated overage of ~USD 420k before credits.

Open items for sign-off:
- Bethany: confirm acceptable max overage cap and whether EdgeTech will accept hosted overflow for seasonal events (we'll add this as a fall-through in the SLA).
- Procurement: confirm PO cadence and PO target date (noted 2026-12-10 in timeline).

If you approve, Priyom will convert the doc to a formal SOW and push to DocuSign.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.docx
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/123456789/ET-4339
